what_its_for: Viloxazine is used to treat Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children (6 years and older) and adults. It helps improve attention, reduce hyperactivity, and control impulsive behavior. This medication is NOT a stimulant, so it is not a controlled substance.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the capsule. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you may carefully open the capsule and sprinkle the contents onto a teaspoon of applesauce. Swallow the mixture right away without chewing. Do not save it for later. Take viloxazine at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to find the best dose for you. For children ages 6–11, the usual starting dose is 100 mg once daily, which may be increased up to 400 mg per day. For teens ages 12–17, the starting dose is 200 mg once daily, which may be increased up to 400 mg per day. For adults, the starting dose is 200 mg once daily, which may be increased up to 600 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store viloxazine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store in a dry place — not in a bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep this medication safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking viloxazine with MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine) — this combination can be very dangerous. Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, because viloxazine can interact with many drugs, especially caffeine, theophylline, and certain seizure medications. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, as it may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Limit alcohol use while taking this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, aggressive or unusual behavior changes, a fast or pounding heartbeat, high blood pressure symptoms (severe headache, blurred vision, chest pain), allergic reactions (rash, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing), or seizures. Contact your doctor for any side effects that bother you, including nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, drowsiness, decreased appetite, or difficulty sleeping.
when_it_works: Viloxazine is not a quick-fix medication. It may take 4 to 6 weeks before you notice the full benefit. Some improvement in ADHD symptoms may be seen within the first 1 to 2 weeks, but the best results usually come with continued use over several weeks. Be patient and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Children under 6 years: Not approved for use in children younger than 6 years old. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of viloxazine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. Older adults: Use with caution — older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Always inform all your healthcare providers that you are taking this medication.
